Notes: Turner 68, specifically its -la- extension represented by the compiled node 68-2x, explicitly cites European Romani angle 'in front' and anglal 'from in front'. The source prints Zargari ānglāl [ānglār] 'from the front' while documenting liquid dissimilation (§2.3.9, p. 128), then āngl-āl 'from the front' (§3.1.15, p. 132). It lists ānglo 'front; in front' as an adverb (§3.20.1.3, p. 143) and 'in front of' as an adposition (§3.20.2.1, p. 144). These are direct matches to the two Turner Romani comparanda, with the source-defined adverbial and ablative forms retained. Original PDF, glyph-decoded source audit and imported key checked; no transcription or identity change. Zargari in front and from the front; source PDF, audit and CDIAL corroborated
